text:
maria nguyen: Noticing repeated p99 blips on the kv path in the latest fifo-load test run. Baseline yesterday with LRU was smooth; after switching to FIFO we see microbursts.
ralph: Yikes — numbers?
maria nguyen: p50 ~6ms, p95 ~12ms, p99 jumps to 190-220ms in short spikes, ~1-3s total region. Happens under sustained 1.2x hotset pressure.
zheng: Any heap growth or GC noise correlated?
maria nguyen: Heap is steady. CPU shows short syscall spikes on evicter threads. Profiling -> top shows syscalls in `madvise` and some page faults around pager.c:handle_page_request.
samir: Can you paste the perf top/snippets?
maria nguyen: Attaching quick dump: 

```
# perf top sample
  17.2%  kv_evicter
  11.1%  pager::touch_page
   9.8%  kv_map::insert_relink
   8.0%  memcpy
   6.6%  futex_wait
```

maria nguyen: Also saw many short back-to-back `munmap`/`mmap` churns from slab compaction in FIFO path.
ralph: Huh — FIFO should avoid reinsert churn, not cause mmap churn. Maybe our FIFO cold-path triggers compaction earlier? Which threshold changed?
zheng: FIFO triggers tombstone reinserts immediately when slot free_count < threshold. LRU delays reinserts until scan. If hotset shifts, FIFO could force more immediate frees and compacting.
samir: That would cause kernel page ops -> latency. Can we repro with `vmstat -s` and `strace -f` on evicter?
maria nguyen: I ran `strace -c` on evicter during an instance: `munmap` count shot up 4000/s during spikes. Also `mincore` returns changed residency bits frequently.
zheng: So fragmentation is getting exposed: FIFO causes earlier slab slicing, increasing address space churn and TLB pressure. That explains memcpy/syscall wall time.
ralph: Quick mitigation: throttle the compaction rate and add backpressure on `reinsert` path. Maybe coalesce frees into a short debounce window.
samir: Agreed. Also consider a small hysteresis: when free_count < X, mark slab as candidate but wait Y ms before aggressive compaction.
maria nguyen: Implemented a local patch adding a 50ms debounce and batching munmap calls. Ran quick load — p99 spikes reduced to 45-60ms, still above LRU baseline but much better.
zheng: Nice. We should also add better telemetry: per-slab munmap/sec, page-fault-rate, and a tracepoint on reinsert->compact cycles.
ralph: For correctness check: any risk the debounce delays reclamation long enough to OOM under extreme pressure?
maria nguyen: Bound debounce with a hard fast-path when free_count hits critical threshold (<=2). Debounce only when moderate pressure.
samir: Good. Next: can we get a perf flame with the patched build and compare callgraphs? Want to confirm syscall/memops reduced.
ci-bot: Deployment scheduled: perf-patch-test -> canary (1 node) at 2026-04-02T15:48:00Z
maria nguyen: Pushed flame graphs: https://perf.internal/graphs/4732109876/fifo-debounce-compare.html
zheng: I see syscall area shrank by ~70% in the evicter sample. But KV insert_relink time increased slightly due to batching. Tradeoff seems acceptable.
ralph: Long-term: re-evaluate FIFO thresholds, maybe adaptive hysteresis driven by page-fault metrics.
samir: Also add unit tests for correctness under racey reinserts; existing tests only cover functional correctness, not timing races.
maria nguyen: I'll open a PR with debounce + telemetry + tests and drop perf numbers in the description. early notes in the PR: "Reduce munmap/mmap churn under FIFO, add slab debounce to avoid microburst latency".
ralph: Thanks — include script to replay the exact load profile for reviewers.
zheng: I'll help with metrics + alert tweaks. If we can detect munmap/sec spike, we can auto-roll back FIFO if mutation exceeds threshold.
maria nguyen: Great. TL;DR: FIFO caused earlier compaction leading to kernel-level page churn -> latencies. Short-term debounce mitigates p99 microbursts; long-term plan is adaptive thresholds and better telemetry. :thumbsup:
